context: Here k=3. From top to bottom, the three rows show the input, the sorted array, and the extracted result. The first row is nums = [1, 7, 6, 3, 2].
description: The first downward arrow reads “Sort the array.” The second row becomes [1, 2, 3, 6, 7]. A blue border and a brace underneath mark the three rightmost elements, 3, 6, and 7.

frames.explanation: The second downward arrow reads “Return the rightmost k elements.” The third row contains only [3, 6, 7], discarding the smaller values 1 and 2. In an ascending array, the largest elements are on the right, so the last k entries suffice.
frames.title: Method 2 (sorting): sort in ascending order and return the rightmost k elements

result: With an O(n log n) sorting algorithm, the total time is O(n log n). This method also sorts the elements that will not be returned.
summary: Sort the entire array in ascending order, then take its last k elements.
title: Method 2 (sorting): sort in ascending order and return the rightmost k elements
